review.logical_form: These are sufficient conditions yielding information values; converses are not asserted.
review.choice_review: The function f and all conditional positive-support coordinates are supplied.

review.domain: P,Q are probability laws on E and phi is a measurable bijection with measurable inverse.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 transports a null witness to F; 1.2 transports the RN density and integrates positive/negative log parts separately, allowing infinite positive part.
review.logical_form: The conclusion is invariance of KL, not a biconditional.
review.choice_review: A1 assumes AC for the RN density; the witness E_0 is one ordinary existential choice.

review.domain: K,L are supplied probability kernels from Z into E,F; Z may be empty.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 constructs each product probability and verifies rectangle evaluations; 2.1 closes the measurable-evaluation class under complement and disjoint union; 3.1 applies pi-lambda.
review.logical_form: This is closure of supplied probability kernels under product, not an iff claim.
review.choice_review: The proof explicitly says it uses no choice: product measures are unique and the measurable-evaluation closure is pointwise.

review.domain: P is a probability law on E times F, with marginals defined by rectangles.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition takes D(P||P_E tensor P_F) in [0,infinity], allowing failure of absolute continuity; it never subtracts entropies.
review.logical_form: This specifies the MI functional without a characterization of its zero set.
review.choice_review: The product reference is canonical; the general KL interface inherits its RN assumption.

review.domain: X,Y,Z are standard-Borel random elements with supplied conditional laws K,L.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 composes P_Z with the product kernel; 2.1 intersects the two conull version-equality sets and uses rectangle uniqueness.
review.logical_form: Existence, uniqueness and version independence are direct conclusions rather than an equivalence.
review.choice_review: A1 supplies regular conditional law interfaces; K,L themselves are supplied, and only two null sets are united.

review.domain: P,Q are probability laws on one measurable space; bounded f and finite partitions form test classes.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.2 uses t1_A in the singular case; 2.1 clips ln r, 2.2 optimizes partition constants, and 3.1 uniformly approximates bounded tests by simple functions.
review.logical_form: Equivalently introduces a second formula for the same divergence; neither formula is a hypothesis-to-conclusion iff requiring a converse.
review.choice_review: A1 assumes AC for RN; the variational approximation is the explicit clipped sequence and finite level-set approximation.

review.domain: X has finite nonempty alphabet S, Y is standard Borel, and K is a supplied conditional law.
review.mathematical_review: The entropy integrand uses -t ln t extended continuously by 0, is measurable and bounded by |S|/e, and is invariant under changing K on a null set.
review.logical_form: This defines conditional entropy and its finite-observation specialization; no biconditional is stated.
review.choice_review: K is supplied; simultaneous version uniqueness and the general entropy interface use the stated standard-Borel background.

review.domain: X is a random element with probability law P_X.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition sets H(X)=D(P_XX||P_X tensor P_X), an extended nonnegative value; a diagonal point mass gives unit RN density.
review.logical_form: This is the definition of law entropy, without an iff characterization.
review.choice_review: Diagonal law and product reference are canonical; the underlying measurable KL definition uses its RN interface.

review.domain: Standard-Borel X,Y,Z have joint probability law and supplied conditional versions K,L.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition compares P_ZXY with the same-Z-marginal conditional-product reference, avoiding subtraction of infinite entropies.
review.logical_form: The conditional-product description defines the reference, not an equivalence claim.
review.choice_review: Conditional versions use the regular conditional-law interface, and the well-definedness supplier explicitly assumes AC.

review.domain: K,L have standard-Borel target E and measurable base Z, possibly empty.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 builds a fixed countable rational-simple test family from a generating algebra; 2.1 integrates each test, and 3.1 takes a countable supremum.
review.logical_form: Measurability of the fiber KL functional is the conclusion; there is no converse condition.
review.choice_review: A1 explicitly assumes AC for the countable generating algebra and RN interface; it is false that all sequence data are merely supplied.

review.domain: The base mu is a probability law on standard-Borel Z and K,L are supplied probability kernels.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition integrates the measurable nonnegative fiber divergence, allowing infinite singular fibers and ignoring changes on mu-null sets.
review.logical_form: This defines conditional KL without a necessary-and-sufficient statement.
review.choice_review: The fiber KL and its measurability supplier inherit AC; no measurable family of RN densities is chosen by this Definition.

review.domain: The remark discusses a Lebesgue density f when its differential entropy integral is defined.
review.mathematical_review: It distinguishes -integral f ln f from law entropy; the uniform density on [0,1] has differential entropy 0 while law entropy can be infinite.
review.logical_form: No equivalence between differential and law entropy is claimed.
review.choice_review: It introduces no family of choices, only two distinct information functionals.

review.domain: X,U have finite nonempty alphabets and Z is standard Borel.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 uses one simultaneous null set for version equality; 1.2 factors each positive joint row and drops zero rows; 2.1 integrates the finite identity.
review.logical_form: Version invariance and an additive entropy chain rule are asserted, without a converse.
review.choice_review: A1 explicitly assumes AC for regular conditional law existence and simultaneous uniqueness.

review.domain: P is a standard-Borel probability law and S is its set of positive singleton atoms.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 bounds atoms of mass >=1/n; 1.2 gives diagonal density 1/p_i when P(S)=1; 2.1 exhibits a product-null diagonal remainder when P(S)<1.
review.logical_form: The cases P(S)=1 and P(S)<1 are exhaustive alternatives, not a biconditional in the Statement.
review.choice_review: A1 assumes AC; countability of the union of finite atom sets and enumeration in 1.2 are actual choice interfaces.

review.domain: X,Y,Z are standard-Borel random elements.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 applies KL's zero criterion to P_XY; 1.2 does so for the conditional-product reference; 2.1 passes between the rectangle identity and bounded-function conditional independence.
review.logical_form: Both zero-information criteria are iff claims; their two implications are proved using equality of laws and the indicator/rectangle argument.
review.choice_review: A1 explicitly carries AC for KL, regular conditional laws and the conditional-independence convention.

review.domain: X,Y,Z are standard Borel and the finite quantizer sigma-algebras increase to the full target sigma-algebras.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 approximates bounded tests in L1(P+Q), 2.1 identifies finite push-forward KL, and 2.2 retains the whole Z sigma-algebra in conditional quantization.
review.logical_form: The claims are monotone limit identities; the assertion about existence of quantizer sequences is not an iff.
review.choice_review: A1 supplies countable generating algebras and conditional laws; finite Boolean algebras give explicit quantizer sequences once generators are fixed.

review.domain: E,F are standard Borel, mu,nu are probability laws, and K,L are supplied probability kernels.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 treats marginal or joint singularity; 1.2 constructs a fiber density on one mu-full set; 2.1 integrates log h=log a+log r with finite negative parts.
review.logical_form: The conclusion is an extended nonnegative additive chain rule, not a biconditional.
review.choice_review: A1 is used for RN representatives and a countable determining algebra; no arbitrary unmeasurable fiberwise RN selection is used.

review.domain: X,Y,Z are standard-Borel random elements with common joint law.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 identifies the product reference's Z-disintegration; 2.1 applies KL chain rule, 3.1 splits over Y, and 4.1 integrates two nonnegative terms.
review.logical_form: This is an additive MI chain rule, without a reverse implication.
review.choice_review: A1 assumes AC for RN divergences and conditional disintegrations; 1.1 selects a regular conditional law using that interface.

review.domain: The binary law has p in [0,1] and Y=X.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 verifies the discrete standard-Borel presentation and handles p=0,1; 1.2 sums the two positive diagonal atoms p/p^2 and (1-p)/(1-p)^2.
review.logical_form: The equality I=H is asserted for this deterministic copy; it is not an iff characterization of all joint laws.
review.choice_review: A1 explicitly assumes AC for the general KL/RN interface, despite the finite computation being explicit.

review.domain: X is a fair bit, Y=X, Z=(X,Y), and W is constant.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 gives conditional point masses and CMI 0 given Z; 1.2 gives two 1/2-to-1/4 ratios and CMI ln2 given W.
review.logical_form: The strict increase under coarsening is an example, with no converse claim.
review.choice_review: A1 carries AC for measurable KL and standard-Borel conditional laws; the witness variables are explicit.

review.domain: Z is uniform on [0,1] and X=Y=0; target alphabet is {0,1}.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 shows K' changes only at the null singleton 0; 2.1 gives infinite fiber KL there and zero elsewhere; 3.1 leaves the joint reference and CMI unchanged.
review.logical_form: Version independence is exhibited by this witness, not by an iff statement.
review.choice_review: A1 carries AC and its countable-choice consequence for the interval measure; the modified kernels are explicit.

review.domain: P is uniform Borel probability on [0,1] and X is the identity.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 makes every singleton null, 2.1 applies the non-atomic law-entropy branch, and 3.1 integrates the identically zero f ln f for f=1_[0,1].
review.logical_form: The example computes H=infinity and h=0, without any necessary-and-sufficient claim.
review.choice_review: A1 assumes AC for KL and countable choice for interval volumes; no nonempty-family selection is made in constructing the identity variable.

review.domain: A is finite and p is a full-support probability vector, so A is nonempty.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 bounds |t ln t| by 2 sqrt(t) near zero; 2.1 writes KL as a finite sum of continuous g(q) minus a linear finite expression.
review.logical_form: Continuity and finiteness on the simplex are conclusions, without a converse.
review.choice_review: No choices occur: g(0)=0 is explicit and each p coordinate is fixed.

review.domain: A has k>=1 letters and n>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 partitions words by their unique empirical type; 2.1 injects types into the first k-1 counts, leaving one empty tuple when k=1.
review.logical_form: This is a partition assertion and upper count bound, not an iff.
review.choice_review: One listing of a finite alphabet is enough to specify the count injection; arbitrary-family choice is unnecessary.

review.domain: A has k>=1 letters, q is a probability vector, and n>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 rounds down nq_i and increases the first r positive fractional parts; 2.1 bounds each error by 1/n, including zero coordinates and k=1.
review.logical_form: The assertion is existence of an approximation with an error bound, not an iff.
review.choice_review: The fixed finite listing and first-r rounding rule explicitly determine every q_n.

review.domain: A is finite nonempty and n>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 sums the product weights to 1; 2.1 factors probabilities of arbitrary coordinate events, setting omitted coordinates to the full alphabet.
review.logical_form: Normalization and mutual independence follow from the product construction; the converse product characterization is not asserted.
review.choice_review: Finite distributivity computes all masses and no selection is involved.

review.domain: A carries a probability vector p and q is an attainable n-type with n>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 makes each word probability zero at a support mismatch; 2.1 otherwise computes the common product mass and multiplies by |T_q|.
review.logical_form: The conclusion is a type probability identity, with a specified infinite-divergence convention, not an iff.
review.choice_review: All words in the finite type class are summed; the proof selects no family of representatives.

review.domain: A has k>=1 letters, n>=1, and q is attainable.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 gives the multinomial count, 1.2 shows the mean integer count is modal under q^n, and 2.1-3.1 turn its probability bounds into the two cardinality bounds.
review.logical_form: The claim is a pair of bounds, not a necessary-and-sufficient characterization.
review.choice_review: The modal argument compares all finite count vectors by explicit factorial ratios, without choosing a maximum from an arbitrary family.

review.domain: A has k>=1 letters, p is normalized, and q is attainable.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 combines the type identity with cardinality bounds when D is finite; 2.1 makes all three values zero for support failure, and k=1 gives all values 1.
review.logical_form: These are two probability bounds, not an iff.
review.choice_review: Finite substitution of the two supplied estimates uses no selections.

review.domain: A is fixed finite with k>=1, and every q is an attainable n-type.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 uses nonemptiness of each attainable fiber to take ln|T_q|; 2.1 bounds the error uniformly by (k-1)ln(n+1)/n and proves it tends to zero.
review.logical_form: The conclusions are logarithmic bounds and uniform convergence, without a converse.
review.choice_review: No representative word is selected: attainability guarantees positive cardinality directly.

review.domain: The theorem works on S=supp p, a finite nonempty set, and Gamma is any subset of Delta(S).
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 sums event type classes; 1.2 rounds an interior q; 2.1 bounds the finite upper sum; 2.2 and 3.2 give the lower bound; 5.1 checks the singleton support.
review.logical_form: Equality of interior and closure infima is a sufficient condition for the limit; no necessity is asserted.
review.choice_review: The fixed rounding rule supplies q_n, and the proof only fixes a single interior point at a time.

review.domain: The example fixes a binary alphabet and n=10, at types (4/5,1/5) and (1/2,1/2).
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 gives count 45 and exponential 5^10/4^8; 1.2 gives count 252 and exponential 1024; 2.1 checks cross-multiplied bounds; 3.1 has a lower-bound endpoint sentence defect recorded separately.
review.logical_form: The computations illustrate inequalities and do not assert a biconditional.
review.choice_review: The finite count computations use factorial formulas, with no selections.

review.domain: Bernoulli p lies in [0,1), threshold a in (p,1], and n>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 treats p=0 and chooses q_n=ceil(na)/n; 1.2 proves divergence increasing above p; 2.2 treats a=1 directly; 4.1 computes 5/16 and the optional Hoeffding comparison.
review.logical_form: The tail exponent formula is an equality, not an iff; matching Sanov infima is used only as a sufficient criterion.
review.choice_review: Only the optional Hoeffding comparison assumes AC; the ceil rounding and finite type calculations are explicit.

review.domain: The counterexample uses n=2 on the binary alphabet at q=(1/2,1/2).
review.mathematical_review: Counterexample 1.1 lists 01,10; 2.1 computes e^(2H)=4, unequal to count 2; 3.1 records endpoint equality at the single word 00.
review.logical_form: The refuted universal equality is not a biconditional.
review.choice_review: Both witness words and the boundary word are explicitly listed.

review.domain: X is explicitly finite nonempty.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition retains zero coordinates and defines support by positivity; normalization sum p_x=1 excludes empty support.
review.logical_form: Probability vector and support are defined predicates, without an iff theorem.
review.choice_review: Finite coordinates are supplied.

review.domain: f is finite convex on (0,infinity), normalized at f(1)=0.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 bounds local secant slopes, 1.2 gives the origin limit through monotone n(x), 2.1 proves continuity, and 3.1 gives the recession limit through monotone r(t).
review.logical_form: Existence of boundary limits and interior continuity are direct consequences of convexity, with no converse.
review.choice_review: The proof fixes real points and uses real infima/suprema, without an indexed choice.

review.domain: f(t)=t ln t is defined for t>0.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 uses f''=1/t>0, 1.2 substitutes s=1/t at zero, and 2.1 uses the unbounded increasing logarithm for the recession limit.
review.logical_form: This verifies generator admissibility and limits, not a biconditional.
review.choice_review: The substitutions are explicit.

review.domain: The order ranges are alpha>1 and 0<alpha<1, with t>0.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1-1.2 establishes power limits; 2.1 computes h''=alpha(alpha-1)t^(alpha-2); 3.1 computes g''=alpha(1-alpha)t^(alpha-2) and the two recession values.
review.logical_form: These are convexity and boundary computations for two families, without converse conditions.
review.choice_review: All generators and substitutions are explicit.

review.domain: P,Q are probability vectors on finite nonempty X and f is a finite normalized convex generator.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition separately assigns q f(0) when p=0<q, p f_infinity when q=0<p, and zero when p=q=0; zero times infinite recession is defined as zero.
review.logical_form: The formula defines f-divergence; its support discussion is not an iff statement.
review.choice_review: The finite sum and singular mass are explicit.

review.domain: P,Q are finite nonempty probability vectors and epsilon is in [0,1].
review.mathematical_review: The Definition infimizes type-II acceptance under a null rejection budget; phi=0 is feasible and the objective set lies in [0,1], so its real infimum exists.
review.logical_form: This is a constrained infimum definition, not a biconditional about tests.
review.choice_review: The explicitly feasible zero test removes any nonempty-choice requirement.

review.domain: X,Y are explicitly finite nonempty.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition requires row sums 1 and computes sum_y(PK)_y=sum_x p_x=1 by finite distributivity.
review.logical_form: This defines stochastic matrices and their action rather than an iff characterization.
review.choice_review: All coordinates and finite row sums are supplied.

review.domain: P,Q share a finite nonempty alphabet.
review.mathematical_review: The KL Definition omits p=0 coordinates, gives infinity when p>0=q, and identifies the t ln t perspective using f(0)=0 and f_infinity=infinity.
review.logical_form: The formula and generator identification are definitional identities, not a biconditional theorem.
review.choice_review: The sum has no choices.

review.domain: Any finite family of nonnegative pairs is allowed, including the empty family.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 handles B=0, including A=0; 1.2 handles ordinary positive-b Jensen and origin limits; 2.1 regularizes singular b coordinates and passes to the recession limit.
review.logical_form: The assertion is perspective subadditivity, with no converse or equality criterion.
review.choice_review: Finite regularization replaces each singular b_i by the same eta, not by a choice of representatives.

review.domain: P,Q share a finite nonempty alphabet; alpha>0 with a separately defined order-one value.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition assigns affinity 0 to singular coordinates below one, infinity above one, and treats zero total affinity as infinite divergence below one.
review.logical_form: These are piecewise definitions of affinity and divergence, with no iff theorem.
review.choice_review: Every term is explicit.

review.domain: P,Q are finite nonempty probability vectors with P<<Q and n>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 multiplies positive support likelihood ratios; 2.1 bounds variance of the centered mean by sigma^2/n and obtains the tail bound sigma^2/(n delta^2).
review.logical_form: The conclusion is convergence in probability and a support identity, not a biconditional.
review.choice_review: The centered variables and all expectations are explicit finite expressions.

review.domain: P,Q and the common kernel have finite nonempty source/target alphabets.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 applies perspective subadditivity at each output y; 2.1 uses positive homogeneity and row sums to recover input divergence, including zero kernel entries.
review.logical_form: The data-processing inequality is one-way and contains no equality characterization.
review.choice_review: There are only explicit finite arrays.

review.domain: P,Q and K satisfy the finite nonempty alphabet conventions.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 identifies t ln t closed-perspective terms with KL including singular support; 2.1 applies f-divergence data processing.
review.logical_form: This states a one-way contraction inequality, not an iff.
review.choice_review: No selections are introduced by specializing the generator.

review.domain: P,Q and K are finite and alpha is positive unequal to one.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 handles alpha>1 through t^alpha-1 and support inclusion; 1.2 uses 1-t^alpha below one; 3.1 handles zero input affinity and reverses the logarithmic inequality.
review.logical_form: Only Renyi data processing is claimed; no converse or equality criterion.
review.choice_review: The two generators are explicit.

review.domain: P,Q are finite nonempty probability vectors.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 differentiates the finite affinity at order one when P<<Q; 1.2 makes the left limit infinite when supported P mass s<1, and 2.1 gives the right singular limit.
review.logical_form: The claim is a two-sided limit identity, without a necessity assertion.
review.choice_review: Finite differentiation and the explicit supported mass s involve no choice.

review.domain: P,Q are finite nonempty probability vectors and epsilon is strictly between 0 and 1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 finds a zero-type-II test under singularity; 1.2 thresholds likelihood at D-delta; 2.1 lower-bounds every feasible test using D+delta; 3.1 squeezes exponents.
review.logical_form: The exponent equality is not an iff condition for a test or law.
review.choice_review: The tests A_n and B_n are explicitly defined finite events.

review.domain: The null P=(2/3,1/3), alternative Q=(1/3,2/3), and epsilon=1/2 are fixed.
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 computes type-I 1/2 and type-II 1/4 for phi=(1/4,1); 2.1 bounds every feasible alternative power by 3/4; 3.1 checks threshold direction.
review.logical_form: This exhibits an optimizer for a fixed experiment, without an iff claim.
review.choice_review: The optimizer is explicit and its comparison is over finite coordinates.

review.domain: The example fixes positive binary P=(3/4,1/4),Q=(1/4,3/4).
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 gives KL=(ln3)/2; 1.2 gives D_1/2=ln(4/3); 1.3 gives D_2=ln(7/3); 1.4 and 2.1 give TV generator divergence 1/2.
review.logical_form: These are numerical evaluations, not biconditionals.
review.choice_review: No selections occur in the fixed two-coordinate calculations.

review.domain: P=(1,0),Q=(0,1) are fixed binary disjoint-support laws.
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.2 gives infinite KL; 2.1 adds f(0)=1/2 and recession=1/2 to get TV 1; 3.1 gives infinite Renyi at all positive orders.
review.logical_form: The example computes boundary values, without an iff characterization of disjointness.
review.choice_review: Both point masses and the generator are explicit.

review.domain: The source has m>=1 strictly positive probabilities and blocks have n>=1.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition explicitly gives the one-symbol source p_1=1; finite distributivity normalizes the product block law and lexicographic order identifies its m^n symbols.
review.logical_form: This defines sources and blocks, without a biconditional theorem.
review.choice_review: The source order and lexicographic block order are explicit.

review.domain: p,q are normalized finite vectors and q_i>0; normalization requires m>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 proves ln t<=t-1; 2.1 sums on positive p support and uses positive q to force full support at equality, then p=q.
review.logical_form: The Statement's zero-KL iff is proved by equality of both inequalities; assigned rows address the other axes.
review.choice_review: No arbitrary-family choice occurs in the explicit logarithmic comparison.

review.domain: p is a full-support finite source.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition divides nats by ln2 and expands -sum p_i log_2 p_i; all logs have positive inputs, including ln1 at a singleton source.
review.logical_form: This fixes entropy units, without a necessary-and-sufficient assertion.
review.choice_review: The unit conversion is termwise and deterministic.

review.domain: Codewords C(i) are nonempty binary words; the extension domain includes the empty source word.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition maps the empty source word to epsilon, requires ell_i>=1, defines UD as injectivity of C*, and gives the finite expected length.
review.logical_form: Unique decodability is a defined predicate, with no theorem asserting an iff between two independent properties.
review.choice_review: C is supplied and its extension is fixed by concatenation.

review.domain: The supplied binary source code has positive codeword lengths on a nonempty alphabet.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition requires nonsingularity and forbids proper prefixes; its trie root is epsilon and its codewords are leaves.
review.logical_form: The conjunction defines prefix code; it is not a biconditional theorem to prove.
review.choice_review: The finite trie is explicitly all prefixes of the supplied codewords.

review.domain: C is uniquely decodable on finite nonempty [m], with ell_i>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 groups K^k by total length and uses distinct concatenations; 2.1 bounds by k(lambda-1)+1; 3.1 takes kth roots and proves their limit is 1.
review.logical_form: McMillan is a necessary inequality for UD codes; sufficiency for UD is not asserted here.
review.choice_review: The max length is over a fixed finite nonempty codebook and counting uses explicit finite sums.

review.domain: The source is full-support, m>=1, and public frame length n>=1.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition begins with [0,1) for the empty prefix, multiplies widths by positive p_i, and picks a midpoint dyadic cell of s=floor(-log_2 w)+2 bits.
review.logical_form: This specifies an encoder; it contains no necessary-and-sufficient characterization.
review.choice_review: Symbol order, interval refinement and midpoint rounding fix every output.

review.domain: C is a prefix code with all codewords nonempty.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 makes an initial codeword unique by prefix comparability; 2.1 repeatedly removes it, decreasing unread length and treating the empty word explicitly.
review.logical_form: Only prefix implies uniquely decodable is asserted; its converse is false and not claimed.
review.choice_review: At each stage the codeword is uniquely forced, so no choice principle is needed.

review.domain: The finite source has m>=1 and the requested lengths are positive integers.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 gets necessity from Kraft on the finite codeword set; 2.1 enumerates requests in symbol order and applies effective allocation for sufficiency.
review.logical_form: The Statement asserts exactly the Kraft iff, with both directions explicitly proved.
review.choice_review: The request enumeration is finite and effective rather than an arbitrary-family selection.

review.domain: The source has m>=1 positive weights and the serial order is supplied.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition returns code 0 for m=1; otherwise each minimum-weight merge uses weight/serial ordering and reduces the active count by one.
review.logical_form: This defines Huffman's procedure and an output contract, not a biconditional theorem.
review.choice_review: All ties and left/right orientations are fixed by serial order.

review.domain: The arithmetic interval source is full-support and n>=1 is fixed.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 partitions [0,1) with positive widths, 2.1 embeds a midpoint dyadic cell, 3.1 deduces prefix-freeness, and 4.1 bounds s by -log_2 p^n+2.
review.logical_form: Prefix-free and lossless are conclusions of this encoder; no converse is asserted.
review.choice_review: Cells and emitted indices are deterministic.

review.domain: Positive integer frequencies q_i sum to Q and 1<=n<=N; a stream has a supplied finite frame count R.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition uses finite registers, n exact endpoint updates, bounded search 0..B, midpoint floor index k, and a finite trie decoder.
review.logical_form: This is a deterministic encoder/decoder procedure, not a biconditional theorem.
review.choice_review: Finite search and trie construction are explicit and have fixed orders.

review.domain: The source is full-support, with a separate m=1 nonempty-codeword branch.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 normalizes Kraft weights; 1.2 realizes positive Shannon lengths when m>=2; 2.1 applies Gibbs for the lower bound; 3.1 handles strict upper bound and singleton equality.
review.logical_form: The claims are coding bounds and a construction, not a converse characterization of codes.
review.choice_review: Finite normalized Kraft weights and a finite positive length list are explicit; Kraft allocation needs no arbitrary choices.

review.domain: The source has m>=1 positive weights and deterministic Huffman serial rules.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 treats m=1; 1.2 proves termination/prefix-freeness; 1.3 obtains a finite minimum; 2.1-4.1 use sibling exchange and contraction; 5.1 completes induction.
review.logical_form: Optimality and termination are conclusions; the theorem does not characterize all optimal prefix codes by an iff.
review.choice_review: The argument chooses only among finite code lengths/trees; the algorithm's ties are explicitly fixed.

review.domain: The ideal arithmetic encoder uses a positive full-support source and n>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 averages the pointwise code bound; 2.1 expands -log p^n as a sum of n single-letter surprisals, giving nH_2+2.
review.logical_form: The conclusion is an expected-length upper bound, not an equivalence.
review.choice_review: Only finite expectation and an explicit product model are used.

review.domain: Positive rational frequencies configure the finite-register encoder and 1<=n<=N.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 tracks scaled intervals; 2.1 bounds the maximal scale and midpoint cell; 3.1 deduces disjoint cells/prefix-freeness; 4.1 bounds all registers and loop lengths.
review.logical_form: These are correctness, termination and size conclusions, without a converse.
review.choice_review: Encoder, finite search and decoder paths are fully specified.

review.domain: Huffman's source has m>=1, with explicit singleton handling.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 obtains the lower bound by prefix implies UD; 2.1 compares with a Shannon code; 3.1 computes entropy 0 and output length 1 for m=1.
review.logical_form: This is a two-sided cost bound with a singleton exception, not a biconditional.
review.choice_review: Comparison uses the finite Shannon-code supplier and no indexed selection.

review.domain: The configured rational arithmetic coder uses a positive source and n>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 averages its pointwise bound; 2.1 adds n identical single-letter entropy expectations.
review.logical_form: The expected-length inequality is sufficient output performance, with no converse assertion.
review.choice_review: The product law and finite expectation are explicit.

review.domain: The example fixes C(1)=0,C(2)=01 on two symbols.
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 notes 0 is a proper prefix; 1.2 forces parsing from the next bit and finite removal; 2.1 computes Kraft sum 3/4.
review.logical_form: This witnesses UD without prefix; it is not an iff claim.
review.choice_review: Each parsing branch is forced by the next unread bits.

review.domain: The rational example fixes frequencies (3,2,1), N=n=2, and block AB.
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 gives (L,W)=(9,6) and interval [1/4,5/12); 1.2 gives u=2,s=4,k=5,B=6; 2.1 embeds [5/16,3/8) and decodes AB.
review.logical_form: It computes one frame and does not assert an equivalence.
review.choice_review: All integer updates and floor computations are explicit.

review.domain: The example fixes the three-symbol source (1/2,1/4,1/4).
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 merges 2,3 and fixes the last tie by serials, yielding 0,10,11; 2.1 computes both expected length and entropy as 3/2.
review.logical_form: This evaluates a particular optimal code, without a converse characterization.
review.choice_review: The serial order uniquely fixes both merges.

review.domain: A is finite nonempty and the source is IID; n>=1 and epsilon>0.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 makes the finite-valued surprisal transforms IID; 2.1 computes mean H and variance V; 3.1 removes zero-support events and applies the finite-variance weak law.
review.logical_form: The conclusion is a probability bound and convergence, not an equivalence.
review.choice_review: The surprisal function is explicitly extended by zero off support.

review.domain: The source is finite IID and epsilon>0; T_n is a finite positive-support set.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 lower-bounds every typical word mass for the cardinality upper bound; 1.2 upper-bounds those masses for the lower bound; 2.1 invokes AEP for delta_n.
review.logical_form: The three typical-set bounds and delta_n convergence are consequences, not iff assertions.
review.choice_review: Finite sums over the entire typical set require no representative choices.

review.domain: p is strictly between 0 and 1 and every X_i equals one Bernoulli variable Z.
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 proves dependence and positive marginal entropy; 2.1 computes the only block masses p,1-p and their normalized logarithms tending to 0.
review.logical_form: This refutes dropping independence from the AEP hypotheses; no biconditional is claimed.
review.choice_review: The single random variable and all its copies are explicit.

review.domain: Finite product laws alternate fair and deterministic marginals in blocks ending at N_k=2^(k^2).
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 normalizes and projects the finite laws, 2.1 makes I_n=F_n ln2/n deterministic, 3.1 gives two endpoint limits, and 4.1 excludes every constant limit.
review.logical_form: The example disproves a general constant information-rate limit without identical marginals; no converse is asserted.
review.choice_review: Only finite products are used; no infinite-product extension is selected.

review.domain: Bernoulli p ranges over [0,1] with n>=1 and epsilon>0.
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 expresses I_n-h as (k/n-p)ln((1-p)/p); 1.2 treats fair and deterministic endpoints; 2.1 counts clipped binomial weights; 3.1 computes V.
review.logical_form: The typical-set equality is a set description derived from an absolute-error inequality, not a biconditional theorem with a separate converse obligation.
review.choice_review: Counts and clipped floor/ceiling endpoints are explicit.

review.domain: The indexed data have positive normalized weights and S is nonempty for the centroid formula.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 makes W_S>0 and centers the weighted sum; 2.1 expands and cancels the cross term; 3.1 proves unique minimization and separately gives zero cost for empty S.
review.logical_form: This is a squared-error identity with its minimization consequence; assigned row concerns endpoints only.
review.choice_review: All weighted sums are finite and explicit.

review.domain: a<b and g is positive normalized C1 on [a,b].
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 gives endpoints G(a)=0,G(b)=1 and positive minimum of g; 2.1 proves strict increase/bijection; 3.1 inverse continuity; 4.1-5.1 prove inverse derivative formulas including one-sided endpoints.
review.logical_form: The theorem proves smooth invertibility and derivative identities, not a biconditional.
review.choice_review: The inverse is unique by strict increase; no family of choices is made.

review.domain: d,k>=1, X is Borel carrying a probability with finite second moment, and centers are finite.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 obtains Borel cells from continuous distance differences; 2.1 uses least minimizing index; 3.1 bounds distortion by twice the second moment plus twice the largest squared center norm.
review.logical_form: Measurability and finite distortion are direct conclusions, not a converse.
review.choice_review: The least-index rule fixes ties.

review.domain: a<b and f,g are positive normalized C1, with N>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 uses strictly increasing phi to partition [a,b] into Borel cells; 2.1 bounds every error by b-a and distortion by (b-a)^2.
review.logical_form: This proves well-defined finite distortion of the specified compander, without a converse.
review.choice_review: Every boundary and reconstruction value is explicitly fixed by phi.

review.domain: N,d,k>=1 and weights are positive normalized.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.2 uses the centroid identity for strict descent, 1.3 gives at most 2^(Nk) possible center tuples, 2.1 counts changed passes, 3.1 proves the stopping fixed point, and 4.1 counts operations.
review.logical_form: Termination and a fixed point are asserted, not equivalence to global optimality.
review.choice_review: The least-index assignment and unchanged empty-cluster rule are deterministic.

review.domain: N,d,k>=1 and weights are positive normalized.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 enumerates exactly k^N assignments; 1.2 compares any nearest assignment after centering; 2.1 sandwiches the retained cost; 3.1 counts exact operations.
review.logical_form: Global optimality of exhaustive enumeration is the conclusion; no converse is claimed.
review.choice_review: All assignments are enumerated in a specified finite order.

review.domain: a<b and positive C1 densities f,g are normalized on [a,b].
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 changes to cumulative coordinates; 1.2 uniformly bounds the cubic remainder; 2.1 sums cell integrals; 3.1-3.2 identify the midpoint integral limit and change back.
review.logical_form: The statement is a high-rate limit for one compact construction, not a characterization of unrestricted optimal quantizers.
review.choice_review: All compander points are specified midpoint values of phi.

review.domain: a<b and f is a positive normalized C1 density; admissible g are also positive normalized C1.
review.mathematical_review: Proof 1.1 makes A and B(g) finite positive, 2.1 uses (z^(1/3)-1)^2(z^(1/3)+2)>=0, 3.1 forces equality pointwise by positivity/continuity, and 4.1 identifies the unique admissible minimizer.
review.logical_form: Unique minimization is asserted and both attainment and uniqueness are shown.
review.choice_review: The formula f^(1/3)/A explicitly specifies the minimizer.

review.domain: The witness is exactly five equally weighted real points and two centers.
review.mathematical_review: Counterexample 1.1 checks strict nearest assignments for (5/2,9), 2.1 checks its unchanged centroids/cost 17/5, and 1.2/3.1 compare centers (1/2,6) of cost 29/10.
review.logical_form: The refuted assertion is universal fixed-point optimality, not a biconditional.
review.choice_review: Both tuples and all squared distances are explicitly given.

review.domain: The example fixes [0,1], f=g=1, and integer N>=1.
review.mathematical_review: Verification 1.1 makes phi the identity and cells equal; 2.1 integrates t^2 over each centered cell to get D_N=1/(12N^2); 3.1 agrees with the high-rate coefficient.
review.logical_form: The exact distortion formula and its limit are evaluations, not iff assertions.
review.choice_review: The cell midpoints are explicit.

review.domain: T>=0; at T>=1 all layers are finite and may be empty.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition explicitly gives the unique empty path of score 1 at T=0, empty edge product 1 at T=1, positive edge weights, and disabled endpoints of zero weight.
review.logical_form: Paths and reachability are defined predicates; there is no biconditional theorem.
review.choice_review: No vertex order is supplied in this Definition; finiteness gives maximum-score attainment when paths exist, without choosing an arbitrary family.

review.domain: S,Y are finite nonempty and observation length T>=1.
review.mathematical_review: The HMM Definition normalizes pi and the A,B rows, uses an empty transition product at T=1, and leaves posterior path mass undefined at zero evidence.
review.logical_form: Sequence MAP is defined by maximizing posterior mass when p(y)>0, without an iff theorem.
review.choice_review: Finite masses and finite hidden paths are explicit.

review.domain: The input is a finite trellis with a supplied total order on each vertex set.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition returns empty path score 1 at T=0; otherwise D uses a maximum with {0}, omits pointers at D=0, checks terminal Q, and traces back through first maximizing predecessors.
review.logical_form: This is an operational recurrence and output procedure, not a biconditional assertion.
review.choice_review: Supplied finite total orders fix predecessor and terminal ties.

review.domain: The input HMM has nonempty S,Y, observation length T>=1, and a supplied state order.
review.mathematical_review: The Definition uses alpha=pi B(y_1), beta=1, includes only positive transition/emission edges, and delegates max-product; no path yields zero-evidence/no-posterior-MAP output.
review.logical_form: The word exactly when specifies edge inclusion in step 2, a defining instruction rather than a mathematical equivalence theorem.
review.choice_review: State order and the delegated Viterbi tie rule determine the selected path.
